headline: Ocean-freight stress is HIGH and easing — 42.8/100; Cape of Good Hope is the lead driver, -20% vs normal

bullets.text: Global Ocean Freight Stress is **42.8/100** (**high**), down 0.7 pts week-over-week. 3 of 28 monitored chokepoints are disrupted.
The biggest driver is **Cape of Good Hope**, running **82.0/day** vs a normal of **103.0/day** (-20%).
**359** changes to the disruption set since the last update.
Also moving now: **Suez Canal** is running **54% below** normal.
Market context: Brent crude **$130.8/bbl** (+7.88% prev_close) — context for the energy-route chokepoints, not a stated cause.
Against the loaded sample trade book, **$372.5M** routes through disrupted lanes — an estimated **$3.2M** cost-of-delay ($1.7M–$5.1M).
